Next.js provides two conventions to handle not found cases: * **`not-found.js`**: Used when you call the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function in a route segment. * **`global-not-found.js`**: Used to define a global 404 page for unmatched routes across your entire app. This is handled at the routing level and doesn't depend on rendering a layout or page. ## `not-found.js` The **not-found** file is used to render UI when the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function is thrown within a route segment. Along with serving a custom UI, Next.js will return a `200` HTTP status code for streamed responses, and `404` for non-streamed responses (see [Status Codes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#status-codes) for details about SEO). ```tsx filename="app/not-found.tsx" switcher import Link from 'next/link' export default function NotFound() { return (

Return Home
) } ``` In the [component hierarchy](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#component-hierarchy), `not-found.js` renders between `loading.js` and `page.js`. It is wrapped by the `` boundary from `loading.js` and the error boundary from `error.js` in the same segment. ## `global-not-found.js` (experimental) The `global-not-found.js` file lets you define a 404 page for your entire application. Unlike `not-found.js`, which works at the route level, this is used when a requested URL doesn't match any route at all. Next.js **skips rendering** and directly returns this global page. The `global-not-found.js` file bypasses your app's normal rendering, which means you'll need to import any global styles, fonts, or other dependencies that your 404 page requires. > **Good to know**: A smaller version of your global styles, and a simpler font family could improve performance of this page. `global-not-found.js` is useful when you can't build a 404 page using a combination of `layout.js` and `not-found.js`. This can happen in two cases: * Your app has multiple root layouts (e.g. `app/(admin)/layout.tsx` and `app/(shop)/layout.tsx`), so there's no single layout to compose a global 404 from. * Your root layout is defined using top-level dynamic segments (e.g. `app/[country]/layout.tsx`), which makes composing a consistent 404 page harder. part.text:
Migration complete. The `pages/` directory is fully removed and the build + typecheck pass.

## What was migrated

**API replacements (Pages Router → App Router):**
| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `_app.js` + `_document.js` | `app/layout.tsx` (renders `<html>`/`<body>`, owns header/nav/footer + `AppProvider`) |
| `next/document` (`Html`/`Head`/`Main`/`NextScript`) | root layout returning `<html lang="en">` directly + `metadata` export |
| `next/head` (`<Head>`) | `metadata` / `generateMetadata` exports + title template |
| `next/router` `useRouter` | `next/navigation` `useRouter` (in client components) |
| `getServerSideProps` | async Server Component + `headers()` + `dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` |
| `getStaticProps` (ISR `revalidate: 60`) | `export const revalidate = 60` |
| `getStaticPaths` (`fallback: 'blocking'`) | `generateStaticParams` (default `dynamicParams` = blocking) |
| `notFound: true` | `notFound()` from `next/navigation` |
| `router.isFallback` loading | `app/blog/[id]/loading.tsx` |
| `pages/404.js` | `app/not-found.tsx` |
| `pages/_error.js` (`getInitialProps`) | `app/error.tsx` + `app/global-error.tsx` (with `reset`) |
| API routes (`req`/`res`, `req.method`/`req.query`/`req.body`) | Route Handlers (`GET`/`POST`/`PUT`/`DELETE`, `NextRequest`/`NextResponse`, async `params`) — 405 is now automatic |

**Types added:** everything is `.ts`/`.tsx` with interfaces (`Post`, `Comment`, `AppContextValue`, handler props/contexts, route params typed as `Promise<{ id: string }>`). A new `components/NavigationButton.tsx` client component preserves the `router.push`/`router.back` button behavior from the original pages.

Build route table confirms parity: `/` dynamic (SSR), `/blog` static w/ 1m revalidate, `/blog/[id]` SSG (10 paths) w/ 5m revalidate + on-demand rendering, and both API routes as dynamic handlers.
